_comment: Owner: Eshan. Concepts from backpropagation to transformers. The owner of an edge's `to` concept writes that edge.

concepts.name: Computational graph
concepts.description: Representing a computation as a DAG of primitive operations so derivatives can be composed locally.

concepts.name: Backpropagation
concepts.description: Computing gradients of the loss with respect to every parameter by applying the chain rule backward through the computational graph.

misconceptions.description: gradients flow forward from the input to the loss
misconceptions.probe: In which direction are gradients propagated during training, and why does that order make the computation efficient?

misconceptions.description: backpropagation is itself the optimizer that updates the weights
misconceptions.probe: What does backpropagation compute, and which algorithm uses that result to change the weights?

concepts.name: Vanishing and exploding gradients
concepts.description: Gradients shrinking or growing exponentially with depth because backprop multiplies many local derivatives.

misconceptions.description: vanishing gradients are caused by a learning rate that is too small
misconceptions.probe: If you increase the learning rate tenfold in a deep sigmoid network, do the early layers stop having vanishing gradients? Explain.

concepts.name: Weight initialization
concepts.description: Choosing initial weight scales (Xavier/Glorot, He) so activations and gradients keep a stable variance across layers.

misconceptions.description: initializing all weights to zero is fine because training will move them apart
misconceptions.probe: What happens to the hidden units of an MLP if every weight starts at exactly zero?

concepts.name: ReLU and its variants
concepts.description: Rectified linear units and variants (leaky ReLU, GELU) whose non-saturating positive region keeps gradients from vanishing.

concepts.name: Batch and layer normalization
concepts.description: Normalizing activations with learned scale and shift to stabilize and speed up training; batch statistics in training versus running statistics at inference.

misconceptions.description: batch normalization uses the current batch statistics at inference time too
misconceptions.probe: At test time a single example arrives. Which mean and variance does a batch-norm layer use, and why?

concepts.name: Dropout
concepts.description: Randomly zeroing activations during training as a regularizer, with rescaling so expected activations match at inference.

misconceptions.description: dropout is still applied when making predictions at inference
misconceptions.probe: Should a trained network randomly drop units when it predicts on the test set? What does inverted dropout do about the scale?

concepts.name: Residual connections
concepts.description: Skip connections that add a block's input to its output, giving gradients an identity path and enabling very deep networks.

misconceptions.description: residual connections help only because they add extra parameters
misconceptions.probe: A residual block adds x to F(x) with no extra weights. Why does that help gradients reach early layers?

concepts.name: Convolutional layers
concepts.description: Sliding learned filters over spatial inputs with weight sharing and local connectivity; kernel size, stride, padding, channels.

misconceptions.description: each output position of a convolution has its own separate weights
misconceptions.probe: How many distinct weights does a 3x3 conv layer with 16 input and 32 output channels have, and how does that depend on image size?

concepts.name: Pooling and CNN architectures
concepts.description: Downsampling with max/average pooling and stacking conv blocks into CNN architectures with growing receptive fields.

concepts.name: Recurrent neural networks
concepts.description: Networks that process sequences with a hidden state updated by shared weights at each time step, trained with backpropagation through time.

concepts.name: LSTM and gated recurrent units
concepts.description: Gated recurrent cells (input, forget, output gates; GRU) whose additive cell-state path mitigates vanishing gradients over time.

misconceptions.description: the forget gate erases memory, so a forget gate value near 1 means forgetting everything
misconceptions.probe: If an LSTM forget gate outputs 0.99, does the cell keep or discard its previous state?

concepts.name: Attention mechanism
concepts.description: Weighting values by the softmax of query-key similarity so a model can focus on relevant inputs; additive and dot-product attention.

misconceptions.description: attention weights are learned parameters fixed after training
misconceptions.probe: Are attention weights the same for every input sentence after training? What actually is learned?

concepts.name: Self-attention and multi-head attention
concepts.description: Attention where queries, keys and values come from the same sequence; scaled dot-product and multiple heads in parallel.

concepts.name: Positional encoding
concepts.description: Injecting token order into permutation-invariant self-attention via sinusoidal or learned position embeddings.

misconceptions.description: self-attention already knows token order without positional encodings
misconceptions.probe: If you shuffle the input tokens of a transformer layer with no positional encoding, how do its outputs change?

concepts.name: Transformer architecture
concepts.description: Encoder/decoder stacks of multi-head self-attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections and layer normalization.
